# Life cycles and vectors

> *A parasite's life cycle sets where it is caught, which stage causes disease, which stage is found in the laboratory, and where control can break the cycle.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Read a life cycle diagram; identify definitive and intermediate hosts and vectors; relate the cycle to diagnosis and control |
| Hosts and vectors | Definitive host, intermediate host, vector; a tree of how parasites reach humans |
| Reading a life cycle | *Plasmodium falciparum* (anchor) as the worked example, drawn as a flow |
| Control | Breaking the cycle: vectors, sanitation, treatment of the human reservoir |
| Scenario questions | Which stage or exposure explains a described infection |
